subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular `scripts/install.sh` architecture now, and what public entrypoint plus helper-loading shape must be required?
rationale: This is not a broken current behavior; it changes the structure of a stable public setup surface whose docs, website publishing, tests, and release validation currently assume one shell script.

options.title: Keep targeted refactors only
options.body: Continue extracting or deleting installer code only when tied to concrete installer bugs, validation gaps, or owner-approved cleanup.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve a module layout only if `openclaw.ai/install.sh` remains a safe single entrypoint and the publish/test matrix changes in the same plan.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide the served shell installer should remain monolithic to avoid helper-loading and packaging risk for `curl | bash`.

recommendation.title: Keep targeted refactors only
recommendation.body: Continue extracting or deleting installer code only when tied to concrete installer bugs, validation gaps, or owner-approved cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent installer-specific fixes and install-smoke work make this the strongest available routing signal for deciding whether the split shape is worth the compatibility cost.
